title: Nature Created Man and Woman as Equals

topics.name: Present perfect and present perfect continuous
Comparison with as ... as / not so ... as

options: Tomba is a lawyer who supports women's rights.
Tomba is a lawyer which supports women's rights.
Tomba is a lawyer whom supports women's rights.
questions.rule: Use the relative pronoun who for a person who does the action.

options: Women are as important than men.
Women are as important as men.
Women are as more important as men.
questions.rule: Equal comparison: as + plain adjective + as.

options: Lanthoi has just finish her homework.
Lanthoi has just finished her homework.
Lanthoi have just finished her homework.
questions.rule: Present perfect: has (singular) + past participle finished.

options: Lanthoi said that I wanted to do something interesting.
Lanthoi said that she wanted to do something interesting.
Lanthoi said that she want to do something interesting.
questions.rule: In reported speech I becomes she and the tense moves back: wanted.

options: Who's article is on the table?
Whose article is on the table?
Whom article is on the table?
questions.rule: Whose asks about the owner; who's means who is.

options: The garden is not so big than the mustard field.
The garden is not so bigger as the mustard field.
The garden is not so big as the mustard field.
questions.rule: Negative equal comparison: not so + plain adjective + as.

options: Lanthoi asked her father why women did not get equal pay.
Lanthoi asked her father why did women not get equal pay.
Lanthoi asked her father that why women did not get equal pay.
questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order and no that: why women did not get ...

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Ashangbi has been writing articles on women's rights since twenty years.
Ashangbi has been writing articles on women's rights for twenty years.
Ashangbi is writing articles on women's rights for twenty years.
questions.rule: An action that started in the past and still goes on: has been writing ... for + period.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A plural subject (both parents) takes have in the present perfect: have shared.

questions.rule: as ... as needs an adjective in the middle: as important as.

questions.rule: After said, the verb is past and agrees with one person, Ashangbi: was.

questions.rule: The pronoun is the subject of writes and refers to a person, so use who.

questions.rule: Present perfect = has + past participle: has shared.

questions.rule: After the past verb asked, will moves back to would.

has + past participle supported with a singular subject.

questions.rule: Your father is right becomes her father was right after told.

questions.rule: Use the interrogative pronoun which to choose between things.
Since morning + still going on: present perfect continuous has been preparing.
A reported request uses requested + person + to + verb.

Reported command: told + person + to + verb.

chat: Have you finished your study, my dear?
questions.rule: With I, use have + past participle: have finished.

chat: Is this your notebook or Lanthoi's?
questions.rule: Possessive pronouns stand alone and never take an apostrophe: hers, mine.

chat: What did your father say about the topic?
options: He said that the world was still full of inequalities.
He said that the world were still full of inequalities.
He said me that the world was still full of inequalities.
questions.rule: The world is singular: was. We say something, but tell someone.

chat: Is your sister taller than you?
options: No, she is not as tall than I am.
No, she is not as taller as I am.
No, she is not as tall as I am.
questions.rule: not as + plain adjective + as: not as tall as I am.

chat: How long have you been practising your speech?
options: I am practising since nine o'clock.
I have been practising since nine o'clock.
I have been practising for nine o'clock.
questions.rule: Present perfect continuous + since + starting time.

options: She is the journalist which writes about women's rights.
She is the journalist who writes about women's rights.
She is the journalist who write about women's rights.
questions.rule: who for a person; it refers to one journalist, so the verb is writes.

chat: What did your teacher ask you this morning?
options: She asked me why I had come late.
She asked me why had I come late.
She asked me why I have came late.
questions.rule: Reported question: statement order + tense moved back: why I had come late.

chat: Why are you so happy today?
options: I have just win the debate at school!
I have just won the debate at school!
I have won the debate at school yesterday!
questions.rule: have just won is right; the present perfect cannot go with yesterday.

questions.source: Lanthoi said, "I am going to speak at the symposium."
options: Lanthoi said that I was going to speak at the symposium.
Lanthoi said that she is going to spoke at the symposium.
Lanthoi said that she was going to speak at the symposium.
questions.rule: I am becomes she was; keep to speak.

questions.source: Tomba is a kind father. He shares all the household chores.
options: Tomba is a kind father which shares all the household chores.
Tomba is a kind father who share all the household chores.
Tomba is a kind father who shares all the household chores.
questions.rule: who replaces He; it refers to one father, so shares.

questions.source: Ashangbi and Tomba are equally busy.
options: Ashangbi is as busy as Tomba.
Ashangbi is as busy than Tomba.
Ashangbi is as busier as Tomba.
questions.rule: equally busy = as busy as.

questions.source: Lanthoi has read many stories about pioneer women.
options: Has Lanthoi readed many stories about pioneer women?
Has Lanthoi read many stories about pioneer women?
Have Lanthoi read many stories about pioneer women?
questions.rule: Move has to the front: Has Lanthoi read ...?

questions.source: Lanthoi said to her mother, "Please spare some time for me."
options: Lanthoi requested her mother to spare some time for me.
Lanthoi requested her mother that spare some time for her.
Lanthoi requested her mother to spare some time for her.
questions.rule: A request becomes requested + person + to + verb; me becomes her.

questions.source: The river is wider than the stream.
options: The stream is not as wide as the river.
The stream is not as wider as the river.
The river is not as wide as the stream.
questions.rule: Swap the two nouns and use the plain adjective: The stream is not as wide as the river.

questions.source: Ashangbi said to Lanthoi, "Have you finished your study?"
options: Ashangbi asked Lanthoi if you had finished your study.
Ashangbi asked Lanthoi if had she finished her study.
Ashangbi asked Lanthoi if she had finished her study.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked if + statement order; have finished becomes had finished.

questions.source: Ashangbi wrote an article. It was printed in every newspaper.
options: Ashangbi wrote an article which it was printed in every newspaper.
Ashangbi wrote an article which was printed in every newspaper.
Ashangbi wrote an article who was printed in every newspaper.
questions.rule: which replaces It (don't keep both) and is used for things.
